knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=A SummarizedExperiment object or matrix containing the expression data ;; f=The network reconstruction function to use, such as netFun (which defaults to Pearson correlation)
- alternatives: None mentioned, but the documentation notes that any network reconstruction algorithm returning a complete, weighted adjacency matrix can be used instead of the default Pearson correlation.
- when_to_use: When you have transcriptomics (or other high-throughput) data from multiple samples and want to reconstruct individual, sample-specific networks to perform downstream statistical analyses (like differential co-expression using limma) or network visualization.
- pitfalls: Reconstructing networks for all genes is computationally expensive and yields extremely large matrices. It is highly recommended to subset the dataset to the most variably expressed genes (e.g., top 500) and pre-filter edges based on condition-specific network differences before running downstream statistical tests on the single-sample edge weights.

workflows.name: single_sample_network_reconstruction
workflows.intent: Reconstruct single-sample co-expression networks from gene expression data and identify differentially co-expressed edges between two patient groups.
input: exp (matrix of gene expression values with genes as rows and samples as columns)
targets (data frame containing sample metadata, specifically sample IDs and group/condition labels)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a SummarizedExperiment object from the expression matrix and metadata. ;; 2. Subset the dataset to the top most variably expressed genes (e.g., top 500) to reduce computational complexity. ;; 3. Construct condition-specific networks and calculate their difference to select highly variable edges. ;; 4. Run the LIONESS algorithm using lioness() to reconstruct single-sample networks. ;; 5. Subset the single-sample network edge weights to the pre-selected highly variable edges. ;; 6. Perform differential co-expression analysis on the edge weights using limma.
workflows.code:
rowData <- DataFrame(row.names = rownames(exp), gene = rownames(exp))
colData <- DataFrame(row.names = targets$sample, sample = as.character(targets$sample), mets = targets$mets)

se <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(counts = as.matrix(exp)), 
                           colData = colData, rowData = rowData)
nsel=500
cvar <- apply(assay(se), 1, sd)
dat <- se[tail(order(cvar), 500), ]
netyes <- cor(t(assay(dat)[, dat$mets == "yes"]))
netno  <- cor(t(assay(dat)[, dat$mets == "no"]))
netdiff <- netyes-netno
cormat2 <- rep(1:nsel, each=nsel)
cormat1 <- rep(1:nsel,nsel)
el <- cbind(cormat1, cormat2, c(netdiff))
melted <- melt(upper.tri(netdiff))
melted <- melted[which(melted$value),]
values <- netdiff[which(upper.tri(netdiff))]
melted <- cbind(melted[,1:2], values)
genes <- row.names(netdiff)
melted[,1] <- genes[melted[,1]]
melted[,2] <- genes[melted[,2]]
row.names(melted) <- paste(melted[,1], melted[,2], sep="_")
tosub <- melted
tosel <- row.names(tosub[which(abs(tosub[,3])>0.5),])
cormat <- lioness(dat, netFun)
corsub <- assay(cormat[which(row.names(cormat) %in% tosel), ])
group <- factor(se$mets)
design <- model.matrix(~0+group)
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(yesvsno = (groupyes - groupno), levels = design)  
fit <- lmFit(corsub, design)
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)
fit2e <- eBayes(fit2)
toptable <- topTable(fit2e, number=nrow(corsub), adjust="fdr")
